name: Saudi States & Saudi Arabia
summary: Three Saudi states in central Arabia: the Emirate of Diriyah (1727–1818), the Emirate of Nejd (1824–1891) and the modern kingdom, united by Ibn Saud and named Saudi Arabia in 1932. Oil made it one of the world’s richest states.

knownFor.label: Diriyah (At-Turaif)
knownFor.note: Mud-brick capital of the first Saudi state, a World Heritage Site.

knownFor.label: Ghawar oil field
knownFor.note: The largest conventional oil field in the world.

knownFor.label: Arabic coffee (qahwa)
knownFor.note: Lightly roasted coffee with cardamom, served to guests.

location.value: Most of the Arabian Peninsula, from Nejd in the centre to the Red Sea and Persian Gulf coasts.
location.source: Wikipedia: Saudi Arabia; Wikipedia: Emirate of Diriyah

terrain.value: Deserts (the Empty Quarter, Nafud), the central Nejd plateau, mountains along the Red Sea.
terrain.source: Wikipedia: Saudi Arabia; Wikipedia: Emirate of Diriyah

climate.value: Hot desert climate; very little rain.
climate.source: Wikipedia: Saudi Arabia; Wikipedia: Emirate of Diriyah

resources.value: Date palms and oasis farming; camels; since 1938 vast oil and gas reserves.
resources.source: Wikipedia: Saudi Arabia; Wikipedia: Emirate of Diriyah

disasters.source: Wikipedia: Saudi Arabia; Wikipedia: Emirate of Diriyah

population.value: A few million around 1930; about 35 million today, including many foreign workers.
population.source: Wikipedia: Saudi Arabia; Wikipedia: Emirate of Diriyah

urbanisation.value: From oasis towns to a very urban country (Riyadh, Jeddah, Mecca, Dammam).
urbanisation.source: Wikipedia: Saudi Arabia; Wikipedia: Emirate of Diriyah

disease.value: The 1918–19 influenza; cholera during pilgrimages in the 19th century; MERS (2012).
disease.source: Wikipedia: Saudi Arabia; Wikipedia: Emirate of Diriyah

migration.value: Millions of foreign workers since the 1970s oil boom; Bedouin settlement in towns.
migration.source: Wikipedia: Saudi Arabia; Wikipedia: Emirate of Diriyah

economicBase.value: Oasis farming, herding and pilgrimage income at first; oil since the 1940s.
economicBase.source: Wikipedia: Saudi Arabia; Wikipedia: Emirate of Diriyah

tradeRoutes.value: The Hajj pilgrimage to Mecca; oil exports by tanker and pipeline.
tradeRoutes.source: Wikipedia: Saudi Arabia; Wikipedia: Emirate of Diriyah

wealth.value: Became very rich after the 1973 oil price rise.
wealth.source: Wikipedia: Saudi Arabia; Wikipedia: Emirate of Diriyah

moneyAndTax.value: The riyal; little income tax; state income mostly from oil (Saudi Aramco).
moneyAndTax.source: Wikipedia: Saudi Arabia; Wikipedia: Emirate of Diriyah

inequality.value: Rich royal family and citizens with state jobs; foreign workers with fewer rights.
inequality.source: Wikipedia: Saudi Arabia; Wikipedia: Emirate of Diriyah

governmentType.value: An absolute monarchy ruled by the House of Saud, based on an alliance with the Wahhabi religious movement (1744).
governmentType.source: Wikipedia: Saudi Arabia; Wikipedia: Emirate of Diriyah

keyRulers.value: Muhammad bin Saud (1727–1765). Abdulaziz ibn Saud (founder of the modern kingdom, 1902–1953). King Faisal. King Abdullah. King Salman. Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman.
keyRulers.source: Wikipedia: Saudi Arabia; Wikipedia: Emirate of Diriyah

succession.value: Kings chosen from the sons, and now grandsons, of Ibn Saud.
succession.source: Wikipedia: Saudi Arabia; Wikipedia: Emirate of Diriyah

institutions.value: The royal court, the religious scholars (ulama), the Consultative Council (from 1992).
institutions.source: Wikipedia: Saudi Arabia; Wikipedia: Emirate of Diriyah

stability.value: The first state was destroyed by Egyptian–Ottoman forces (1818); the second fell to the Rashidis (1891); the 1979 siege of the Grand Mosque.
stability.source: Wikipedia: Saudi Arabia; Wikipedia: Emirate of Diriyah

eliteConflict.value: Rivalries inside the royal family; the 2017 anti-corruption detentions.
eliteConflict.source: Wikipedia: Saudi Arabia; Wikipedia: Emirate of Diriyah

armyAndTech.value: Camel cavalry and the Ikhwan religious warriors; today a well-equipped modern military.
armyAndTech.source: Wikipedia: Saudi Arabia; Wikipedia: Emirate of Diriyah

majorWars.value: Wars of unification (1902–1932), the Ikhwan revolt (1927–30), the Gulf War (1991), intervention in Yemen (since 2015).
majorWars.source: Wikipedia: Saudi Arabia; Wikipedia: Emirate of Diriyah

territoryChange.value: Took Riyadh (1902), al-Hasa (1913), Ha’il (1921) and the Hejaz with Mecca and Medina (1925).
territoryChange.source: Wikipedia: Saudi Arabia; Wikipedia: Emirate of Diriyah

alliancesRivals.value: Close ties with the US since 1945; rivalry with Iran.
alliancesRivals.source: Wikipedia: Saudi Arabia; Wikipedia: Emirate of Diriyah

inventions.value: Desalination of seawater on a huge scale.
inventions.source: Wikipedia: Saudi Arabia; Wikipedia: Emirate of Diriyah

scienceEducation.value: Rapid growth of schools and universities since the 1950s.
scienceEducation.source: Wikipedia: Saudi Arabia; Wikipedia: Emirate of Diriyah

openness.value: Conservative and closed until recent reforms (women allowed to drive, 2018; tourist visas, 2019).
openness.source: Wikipedia: Saudi Arabia; Wikipedia: Emirate of Diriyah

communicationTransport.value: Camels until the 20th century; the Hejaz Railway (1908) reached Medina; today motorways, airports and the Haramain high-speed railway (2018).

religion.value: Sunni Islam in the Wahhabi tradition; guardian of Mecca and Medina.
religion.source: Wikipedia: Saudi Arabia; Wikipedia: Emirate of Diriyah

languageWriting.source: Wikipedia: Saudi Arabia; Wikipedia: Emirate of Diriyah

artsArchitecture.value: Najdi mud-brick architecture; poetry (nabati); modern skyscrapers.
artsArchitecture.source: Wikipedia: Saudi Arabia; Wikipedia: Emirate of Diriyah

socialStructure.value: Tribes and the royal family; a large share of foreign workers.
socialStructure.source: Wikipedia: Saudi Arabia; Wikipedia: Emirate of Diriyah

sharedIdentity.value: Identity based on Islam, the royal family and the tribes of Arabia.
sharedIdentity.source: Wikipedia: Saudi Arabia; Wikipedia: Emirate of Diriyah

dailyLife.value: Mud-brick houses in Najd, coral houses on the Red Sea, Bedouin tents; dates, rice (kabsa) and coffee.

neighbours.value: Ottoman Empire (until 1918), Yemen, Oman, Kuwait, Jordan, Iraq.
neighbours.source: Wikipedia: Saudi Arabia; Wikipedia: Emirate of Diriyah

ideasReligions.value: Spread its Islamic teachings abroad with oil wealth.
ideasReligions.source: Wikipedia: Saudi Arabia; Wikipedia: Emirate of Diriyah

colonisation.value: Never colonised by Europeans; the Ottomans and Egyptians fought the first state.
colonisation.source: Wikipedia: Saudi Arabia; Wikipedia: Emirate of Diriyah

riseSignals.value: The 1744 pact between Muhammad bin Saud and the preacher Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab.
riseSignals.source: Wikipedia: Saudi Arabia; Wikipedia: Emirate of Diriyah

peakPeriod.value: Unification under Ibn Saud and the oil boom.
peakPeriod.source: Wikipedia: Saudi Arabia; Wikipedia: Emirate of Diriyah

declineSignals.value: Defeats in 1818 and 1891 ended the first two states.
declineSignals.source: Wikipedia: Saudi Arabia; Wikipedia: Emirate of Diriyah

outcome.source: Wikipedia: Saudi Arabia; Wikipedia: Emirate of Diriyah

sources.value: Wikipedia: Saudi Arabia; Wikipedia: Emirate of Diriyah; Vassiliev, The History of Saudi Arabia (2000).
sources.source: Wikipedia: Saudi Arabia; Wikipedia: Emirate of Diriyah

overallCertainty.value: Well documented after 1900; earlier dates are approximate.
overallCertainty.source: Wikipedia: Saudi Arabia; Wikipedia: Emirate of Diriyah
